```python
.sort("sold_at")
.unique(subset=["store_id", "receipt_no"], keep="last", maintain_order=True)
```

Sorting ascending and keeping the last row gives the latest `sold_at` per pair. Null `sold_at` values sort first, so a non-null timestamp wins over a null one. If two rows tie on `sold_at`, the later one in the input is kept. Tell me if you want a different tiebreak.
